problem: Prior instruction-following agents rely on scripted, hard-coded teachers (e.g., the correction module of Co et al.) that are not scalable or interactive, while emergent-language work usually yields uninterpretable protocols.
motivation: Agents that cooperate with humans need interactive guidance rather than static supervision. The paper asks whether a trained agent can learn a discrete, emergent, yet interpretable and reusable guidance language that speeds up new learners without extra supervision.
key_idea: Insert a Gumbel-softmax discrete message bottleneck in a pretrained Guide agent, and feed its messages to a new Learner, so that the Guide learns a grounded emergent language that accelerates learning.
insight: The Guide's messages are highly correlated with actions (and with observations such as target position), so the language is interpretable. Guides pretrained on one level or on multiple levels help nearly as much as a level-specific Guide (Figs. 2-3), suggesting the messages encode general skills. CIC decreases over training, showing that Learners become less dependent on guidance. The messages are strongly tied to the Guide's actions, and hijacking them yields 72-76% obedience.
method: Learner: BabyAI baseline (GRU instruction encoder, CNN observation encoder, FiLM, memory LSTM, 2-layer policy) trained by behavioral cloning.

Guide: same architecture plus a bottleneck between the memory LSTM and the policy; a GRU decoder emits a length-2 message over 3 tokens (9 messages), discretized with a straight-through Gumbel softmax, then re-encoded by a GRU before the policy.
Guidance channel: a new Learner gets a fresh GRU encoder for the Guide's messages as extra input to its policy; the pretrained Guide is finetuned jointly.
Training: three stages: PPO RL expert to produce demonstrations; imitation-learn Learner baseline and Guide separately; then train new Learner plus pretrained Guide.

Analysis: message-action and observation-message conditional distributions, Causal Influence of Communication (CIC) metric, and 'hijacking' the Guide to send hand-picked messages (pirouette, waltz, obedience).

setting.backbone: BabyAI Learner/Guide (GRU + CNN + FiLM + LSTM, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Demonstrations from PPO-trained RL experts on six BabyAI levels (GoToObj, GoToLocal, GoToObjMaze, PickupLoc, PutNextLocal, GoTo); imitation learning
setting.observation: partially observable 7x7x3 egocentric grid view + language instruction
setting.action_space: discrete BabyAI primitive actions (turn, forward, pickup, drop, toggle)
setting.privileged: none at test time for the Learner; the pretrained Guide is used as the guidance source

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are in BabyAI learning curves and epochs-to-90%-success (Table 1), which don't match the canonical benchmarks.
results: On all six BabyAI levels, a Learner with a pretrained Guide reaches 90% validation success in fewer epochs than the baseline (e.g., PickupLoc 1 vs 8, PutNextLocal 2 vs 14, GoTo 12 vs 20). Guides transfer to harder unseen levels and a multi-level Guide matches single-level Guides. Sending hand-crafted messages gives 76% (GoToObj) and 72% (GoToLocal) obedience.
limitations: Only BabyAI gridworld with a small vocabulary (3 tokens, length 2) and imitation learning; no real navigation benchmark or RL.
Messages are strongly correlated with the Guide's own actions, i.e., they act like action suggestions rather than general-purpose guidance.
Guidance speeds up learning but does not improve final performance; the finetuned Guide's messages do not work with the old policy.
builds_on: Co et al. 2018 guiding correction module
